mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading UNRATE in predicting SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% month-over-month suggests accelerating economic demand, which typically precedes equity market optimism and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO momentum and SPX 5-day forward returns (R-squared < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months indicates a cooling demand environment, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite CPIAUCSL below 3% for the required horizon (p < 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (i.e., rates rise), the discount rate applied to future cash flows increases, which tends to depress equity valuations and result in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show a positive beta to 12-month FEDFUNDS change (beta > 0, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates labor market imbalance that boosts investor sentiment, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: No significant interaction effect detected in OLS regression (p > 0.05 for joint significance).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling industrial production (INDPRO) below trend for four consecutive months suggests structural supply-side weakness, which often precedes equity market corrections and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO below trend for four consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns remain non-negative despite the identified supply weakness (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (indicated by FEDFUNDS < 1.00% for two consecutive months), the equity discount rate is expected to decline, supporting higher future earnings valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 1.00% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no significant relationship with FEDFUNDS level during the easing period (p > 0.05).
